column1: # Agent versions with a published security fix. One line each, tab separated. After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
#   id        what lines of the same tool share: they make one row in the report, which shows the hole
#             of each line the installed version falls under and says to update to the highest of
#             their fixed versions, or to a later fix when another line of the tool covers that one
#   name      as the report shows it
#   os        all, mac, linux or win (win is Git Bash and gird-check.ps1)
#   kind      plist   an Info.plist's CFBundleShortVersionString (an XML plist; a binary one is not read)
#             folder  the highest version-named folder in a folder
#             npm     a package's package.json in the global npm installs and npx's cache
#             mcparg  name@version in the MCP configs section 2 reads
#   where     plist and folder: a path, with the path tokens of data/sessions.tsv or an absolute path.
#             npm and mcparg: the package name
#   affected  <fixed, or >=first <fixed
#   hole      what the hole allows, a few words from the advisory
#   advisory  the advisory's https link
# Lines of one tool agree on its name, and lines of one advisory on its range and hole. Each tool has a
# line for its newest fix, and the version a row says to update to is never in another line's range, so
# it has no published fix of its own; an older advisory may have a line too, for what its hole allows.
# Versions compare part by part as numbers. A version that is not numbers and dots is not reported.
# Each tool's advisories were read in October 2026 from its vendor's repository, GitHub's global
# database and OSV: a repository can publish one that neither of the other two lists.
# Cursor is read on macOS only: its version file on the other systems was not verified. Its newest fix
# with a version is 3.1.2, for Cursor on macOS (GHSA-p9g2-cr55-cw9c, of the 33 advisories in
# cursor/cursor). Claude Code: anthropics/claude-code publishes 31 advisories for the npm package, and
# two of them are in neither GitHub's global database nor OSV. The newest fix is 2.1.260, from 2.0.68
# (GHSA-gfvf-j8jh-jxxw, one of the two); below 2.0.68 the highest fix is 2.1.179 (GHSA-pq7j-f95f-qfcv),
# in its range, so the row says 2.1.260 there too. GHSA-9f65-56v6-gxw7 and the sandbox escape
# GHSA-7835-87q9-rgvv have lines for what their holes allow. mcp-remote: GHSA-6xpm-ggf7-wc3p is its
# only advisory, and its repository publishes none.
# Amazon Q: the version folder is the language server's (Language Servers for AWS), which the bulletin
# fixes in 1.69.0 (aws/language-servers publishes the bulletin's two advisories, and no later bulletin
# names it). The extension's own version is not read. Amazon Q keeps the server in
# aws/toolkits/language-servers/AmazonQ under ~/Library/Caches, ~/.cache or %LOCALAPPDATA%: so says
# its own code, Amazon-Q-Developer/amazon-q-vscode, which the 2.8.0 extension names as its source, and
# so does that build. The aws/language-servers/<name> folder of aws-toolkit-vscode is the AWS
# Toolkit's own; that repository has carried no Amazon Q code since January 2026.
# id
